summary: The paper introduces a controlled, ground-truth-exact testbed for evaluating cheap training-free uncertainty-quantification (UQ) signals — mean max-token-probability, negative predictive entropy, and self-consistency, plus a logistic combination and a hidden-state probe — using a tiny (~50K-parameter) from-scratch transformer trained on integer addition, sidestepping the LLM-judge confound present in most open-domain QA UQ evaluations. On the main seed=0 run (65.4% accuracy) all training-free signals discriminate well (AUROC 0.84-0.87), self-consistency is measurably overconfident (ECE 0.088, fixable via recalibration or combination), and confidence-based abstention raises retained-set accuracy to 81-90% depending on coverage. This third revision responds to round-2 reviewers by adding a new mid-scale (~31%-accuracy) 3-seed sweep, finding that self-consistency's seed-to-seed variance — previously the highest of all signals in a near-degenerate ~3%-accuracy sweep — becomes the lowest of the five signals at higher accuracy, suggesting the earlier instability was substantially an artifact of the near-random-accuracy regime. The paper also corrects a table transcription error and explicitly flags two remaining gaps: no seed sweep at the main run's own 65%-accuracy scale, and no bootstrap/DeLong CI on the single-seed headline AUROC gaps.
strengths:
- I independently reran experiment.py end-to-end (not just spot-checked the JSON) and it reproduced every headline number exactly: overall accuracy 0.6535, all four AUROCs to 4 decimal places (0.8712610547002948, 0.8630505513702369, 0.840786112020963, 0.8741871383338793), the digit/carry accuracy breakdowns, and even the wall-clock time (438.2s, matching the paper's stated 438s exactly) — this is unusually strong reproducibility for a submitted paper.
- The mid-scale sweep's numbers (robustness_midscale_results.json) match Table in Sec. 3 to full precision (e.g. self-consistency std 0.01839 -> reported 0.018, mean-max-prob std 0.02056 -> 0.021), and the reduced-scale sweep's corrected neg-mean-entropy minimum (0.8384 in the JSON) matches the paper's corrected 0.838, confirming the transcription fix is accurate.
- The paper is candid about its own limitations across three review rounds — it names unresolved gaps precisely (no full-scale seed sweep, no bootstrap CI), hedges the mid-scale finding appropriately ("consistent with... though does not conclusively prove"), and the ground-truth-exact synthetic design is a genuinely useful methodological contribution cleanly motivated against the semantic-entropy/LLM-judge literature (Kuhn et al. 2023; Farquhar et al. 2024).
weaknesses:
- The paper's own central open question from round 2 — whether self-consistency's seed-instability is a near-degenerate-accuracy artifact or persists at the 65%-accuracy regime the headline numbers actually come from — is still unresolved. The paper itself states the definitive experiment (a multi-seed sweep at full scale) would cost only ~20 additional minutes of CPU time, which is well inside typical review-cycle compute budgets, so leaving it as "future work" for a third consecutive round undercuts the credibility of that framing.
- The headline single-seed ranking (mean-max-prob 0.871 > entropy 0.863 > self-consistency 0.841) still has no significance test attached three rounds after this was first requested, despite the paper acknowledging a bootstrap CI would only require reusing already-collected eval-set predictions (no retraining). The gaps between these three numbers (0.008-0.030) are exactly the kind of thing that could vanish under a CI, and the paper's text ("mean-max-prob... slightly ahead of entropy") still reads as a ranking claim without that support.
- The generalizability of the qualitative finding (self-consistency variance shrinks with accuracy) rests on a single synthetic task and one tiny architecture; the paper appropriately scopes itself as a methods contribution rather than a claim about frontier LLMs, but no second task with a different error structure has been added despite being flagged as a suggestion in round 2.
questions:
1. Given the paper itself estimates the full-scale (65%-accuracy) seed sweep at only ~20 minutes of additional CPU time, what specifically prevented running it this round, given it directly answers the paper's own stated central open question?
2. Similarly, the bootstrap/DeLong CI requires no new training, only reuse of existing eval-set predictions — why does this remain undone after being flagged in round 2?
3. Is there a reason to expect the self-consistency variance-vs-accuracy relationship is monotonic, or could it re-diverge near ceiling accuracy where the correct/incorrect label balance shifts again?
